fi-chitala-chitala.title: Chitala chitala
fi-chitala-chitala.summary: The Indian featherback, Chitala chitala, is a very large notopterid probably restricted to Pakistan, India, Nepal and Bangladesh. Its name has been widely misapplied in the trade, most often to the…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. An obligate, typically nocturnal, predator feeding on smaller fishes, crustaceans and other invertebrates in nature but in most cases adapting well to dead alternatives in captivity.
Although often reported to range throughout most of southern Asia this species is probably restricted to the Indian subcontinent in Pakistan, India (records from the states of…
notes: Prefers dim lighting and access to refuges in the form of driftwood, large rocks or lengths of plastic piping.

A large, mature filter system, rigorous maintenance regime comprising weekly water changes of 50-70% tank volume, and provision of highly-oxygenated water with a degree of movement should be considered mandatory.

fi-apteronotus-albifrons.title: Black Ghost Knife
fi-apteronotus-albifrons.summary: The black ghost knifefish, Apteronotus albifrons, is a weakly electric knifefish from the upper half of South America, from Colombia to Paraguay. Usually sold at around 4 inches, it grows to 50 cm…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Predator / carnivore. A predator that feeds mainly on insects and worms in nature.
It has a widespread distribution throughout the upper half of South America, having been recorded in Ecuador, Colombia, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana, Venezuela, Peru,…
notes: The choice of decor itself isn't critical, although the fish does appreciate plenty of cover.
Large stones and pieces of bogwood, twisted roots, and live plants can all look good.

fi-gymnarchus-niloticus.title: Aba Aba Knife
fi-gymnarchus-niloticus.summary: The aba aba, Gymnarchus niloticus, is a large predatory fish from much of the northern half of Africa, and the only species in its genus. An extended dorsal fin gives it the alternative name…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Has a huge natural range, being present throughout much of the northern half of Africa.
notes: Prefers a dimly lit tank with areas of dense planting, large pieces of driftwood and twisted roots for cover.
Any decor must obviously be weighted down securely.

fi-xenomystus-nigri.title: Black African Knife
fi-xenomystus-nigri.summary: The African knifefish, Xenomystus nigri, is a notopterid recorded from numerous African rivers, including the Nile, Congo and Niger systems. Its swim bladder acts as an accessory breathing organ, and…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Has a diffuse natural distribution covering parts of Nigeria, Cameroon, Democratic Republic of Congo, Egypt, Chad, Liberia, Gabon, Togo, Sudan, Benin, Sierra Leone and Angola.
notes: Ideally the tank should contain some areas of dense planting.
At the very least provide dim lighting and cover in some shape or form.
[ edit ] This species is sometimes available as an aquarium fish, and has been popular in the hobby for a long time.

rows: Up to about 26.9 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)
